main.title: Turing describes a universal model of computation
main.summary: Alan Turing introduced a mathematical model of computation in his 1936 paper On Computable Numbers.

cards.heading: Turing describes a universal model of computation
cards.text: Alan Turing introduced a mathematical model of computation in his 1936 paper On Computable Numbers. Imagine a head reading symbols on a tape divided into cells. A table of rules tells it what to write, which direction to move and when to stop, depending on its current state and the symbol it finds. This spare arrangement can implement any computer algorithm. By reducing calculation to a sequence of defined operations, Turing supplied a way to investigate what an algorithm could compute.

main.title: A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits
main.summary: Claude Shannon's 1937 master's thesis linked Boolean algebra to relay circuits, laying foundations for digital circuit design.

cards.heading: A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits
cards.text:
A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits is the title of a master's thesis written by computer science pioneer Claude E. Shannon while attending the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) in 1937, and then published in 1938. In his thesis, Shannon, a dual degree graduate of the University of Michigan, proved that Boolean algebra could be used to simplify the arrangement of the relays that were the building blocks of the electromechanical automatic telephone exchanges of the day. He went on to prove that it should also be possible to use arrangements of relays to solve Boolean algebra problems. His thesis laid the foundations for all digital computing and digital circuits.

The utilization of the binary properties of electrical switches to perform logic functions is the basic concept that underlies all electronic digital computer designs. Shannon's thesis became the foundation of practical digital circuit design when it became widely known among the electrical engineering community during and after World War II.

main.title: Guernica
main.summary: Pablo Picasso painted Guernica in 1937 after German and Italian forces bombed the Basque town on 26 April.

cards.heading: Guernica
cards.text: Pablo Picasso painted Guernica in 1937 after German and Italian forces bombed the Basque town on 26 April. Across an enormous canvas in grey, black and white, a wounded horse, screaming women, a dead child, a fallen soldier and flames convey the suffering of violence. The painting was shown in the Spanish pavilion at the Paris International Exposition, then toured to raise money for Spanish war relief. Now exhibited at Madrid's Museo Reina Sofía, it became one of the most widely recognised anti-war paintings.

main.title: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
main.summary: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs premiered in Los Angeles on 21 December 1937, bringing Disney's animated fairy tale to feature length.

cards.heading: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
cards.text: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs premiered in Los Angeles on 21 December 1937, bringing Disney's animated fairy tale to feature length. Produced by Walt Disney from the Brothers Grimm story, it was the first American animated feature and the first made with cel animation. David Hand supervised a team of sequence directors. The project overcame doubts within the film industry to become a critical and commercial success. Its initial international earnings exceeded $8 million against a production cost of $1.5 million, demonstrating the audience for feature-length animation.

main.title: The Hobbit
main.summary: The Hobbit was published in 1937, taking the home-loving Bilbo Baggins from his quiet surroundings into Middle-earth.

cards.heading: The Hobbit
cards.text: The Hobbit was published in 1937, taking the home-loving Bilbo Baggins from his quiet surroundings into Middle-earth. Gandalf and thirteen dwarves enlist him to help reclaim their home and treasure from the dragon Smaug. Each stage of the journey introduces new dangers, asking Bilbo to rely on wit and common sense as his confidence grows. Tolkien's episodic adventure earned critical praise and became a classic of children's fantasy. Its appeal rests in the changing relationship between a reluctant traveller and a world far larger than his home.

main.title: Nuclear fission
main.summary: Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann established that a uranium nucleus had split in December 1938.

cards.heading: Nuclear fission
cards.text: Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann established that a uranium nucleus had split in December 1938. Lise Meitner and Otto Robert Frisch explained the result theoretically the following month, and Frisch called the process fission. Splitting a heavy nucleus releases energy along with smaller nuclei, often neutrons and gamma rays. In February 1939, Hahn and Strassmann predicted the release of additional neutrons. That opened the possibility of a chain reaction, in which particles from one split could trigger further splits in sufficient fissile material.

main.title: The War of the Worlds
main.summary: "The War of the Worlds" was a Halloween episode of the radio series The Mercury Theatre on the Air which was broadcast live at 8 pm ET on October 30, 1938 over the CBS Radio Network.

cards.heading: The War of the Worlds
cards.text:
"The War of the Worlds" was a Halloween episode of the radio series The Mercury Theatre on the Air which was broadcast live at 8 pm ET on October 30, 1938 over the CBS Radio Network. The episode was directed and narrated by Orson Welles as an adaptation of H. G. Wells' novel The War of the Worlds and is infamous for inciting a panic by convincing some members of the listening audience that a Martian invasion was actually taking place.

The first half of the program was delivered in a realistic "breaking news" format. Since the Mercury Theatre on the Air had few commercial interruptions, the first break came after fictional reporters had described a devastating alien invasion and the fall of New York City. This apparently caused some confusion and fear among its listeners, though the scale of the panic is disputed.

main.title: Gone with the Wind
main.subtitle: Scarlett O'Hara holds onto Tara as the world around it changes
main.summary: Gone with the Wind follows Scarlett O'Hara through the American Civil War and Reconstruction. Vivien Leigh plays a determined Georgia plantation owner's daughter whose attachment to Tara survives the collapse of her earlier life. Produced by David O. Selznick, directed by Victor Fleming and released in 1939, the film adapts Margaret Mitchell's novel on an unusually expansive scale.

cards.heading: Scarlett and Tara
cards.text: Gone with the Wind follows Scarlett O'Hara through the American Civil War and Reconstruction. Vivien Leigh plays a determined Georgia plantation owner's daughter whose attachment to Tara survives the collapse of her earlier life. Produced by David O. Selznick, directed by Victor Fleming and released in 1939, the film adapts Margaret Mitchell's novel on an unusually expansive scale.

cards.heading: Survival and attachment
cards.text: Scarlett's pursuit of Ashley Wilkes and her difficult relationship with Rhett Butler run alongside battles, displacement and the struggle to preserve her family home. The production makes these upheavals visible through colour, crowded scenes and large settings, while Max Steiner's recurring Tara theme gives her attachment to the land a musical form. Her resourcefulness keeps the story moving, but the choices she makes for security often damage the relationships she believes will make her happy.

cards.heading: A landmark inside a segregated industry
cards.text: The film's romantic view of the slaveholding South and its racial stereotypes are part of its historical legacy. Hattie McDaniel's performance as Mammy brought the first competitive Oscar awarded to a Black performer in 1940. At the segregated ceremony, she and her guest were seated apart from the film's other nominees. The distinction and the treatment she received reveal both the visibility her work achieved and the barriers surrounding that achievement in Hollywood.

main.title: The Wizard of Oz
main.summary: The Wizard of Oz brought L. Frank Baum's fantasy to the screen as an MGM musical in 1939.

cards.heading: The Wizard of Oz
cards.text: The Wizard of Oz brought L. Frank Baum's fantasy to the screen as an MGM musical in 1939. Judy Garland led a cast directed primarily by Victor Fleming, with music by Harold Arlen, lyrics by Yip Harburg and a score adapted by Herbert Stothart. Three-strip Technicolor helped give its imagined world a distinctive presence. The film received five Academy Award nominations, winning for Over the Rainbow and Stothart's score. Garland also received an Academy Juvenile Award, linking its musical achievement to the performance at its centre.

main.title: World War II
main.summary: World War II, or the Second World War (1 September 1939 – 2 September 1945), was a global conflict between two coalitions: the Allies and the Axis powers.

cards.heading: World War II
cards.text:
World War II, or the Second World War (1 September 1939 – 2 September 1945), was a global conflict between two coalitions: the Allies and the Axis powers. Nearly all of the world's countries participated, with many engaging in total war on an unprecedented scale. World War II was the deadliest conflict in history, causing the deaths of 60 to 75 million people, a majority of whom were civilians. Millions died as a result of massacres, starvation, disease, and genocides, including the Holocaust. After the Allied victory, Germany, Austria, Japan, and Korea were occupied, and German and Japanese leaders were tried for war crimes.

The causes of World War II included unresolved tensions in the aftermath of World War I and the rise of fascism in Europe and militarism in Japan. Key events preceding the war included Japan's invasion of Manchuria in 1931, the Spanish Civil War, the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War in 1937, and Germany's annexations of Austria and the Sudetenland.
